name: nemotron-pipeline
goal: Multi-stage pipeline: PM → Parallel Architects → Judge → Coder → Reviewer → Release Gate

tasks.description: Create technical specification with acceptance criteria
tasks.prompt:
## Tech Lead PM Invocation

### User Request
Create a blackjack game in Python for Linux terminal with these requirements:
- No external dependencies (stdlib only)
- Single file
- Clean architecture and code principles
- Professional, good-looking terminal UI
- Human-readable code

### Instructions
Produce a structured technical specification with measurable acceptance criteria and environment constraints. Query the scout agent for any necessary codebase facts before finalizing.

### Output Format
Return a Spec Packet with:
- Goal (one sentence)
- Scope (In/Out)
- Assumptions & Clarifications
- Environment Constraints (e.g., Static analysis only, no live runtime)
- Acceptance Criteria table (ID, Criterion, Verification Method)
- Work Breakdown table (Task ID, Name, Description, Acceptance Ref, Dependencies, Complexity)
- Critical Path & Risks (Crux, Mitigation, Unknowns)
- Questions for User (numbered list, if any ambiguities block completion)
- Handoff Notes for Downstream

phases.title: Architecture Ideation

tasks.prompt:
## Architect Invocation (Minimal-Diff Strategy)

### Spec Packet
The specification from the previous 'requirements' phase will be provided as context.

### Strategy
minimal-diff

### Instructions
Propose a minimal-diff architectural approach. Reuse existing code, avoid new abstractions, smallest change set. Query the scout agent for existing patterns, interfaces, and dependencies. Return an Architecture Design Doc with: Strategy, Goal Restatement, High-Level Approach, Component Diagram, File Change Plan, Data Models & Schemas, API/Interface Definitions, Key Algorithms (pseudocode), Dependency Changes, Configuration Changes, Error Handling & Failure Modes, Concurrency & State Considerations, Security Considerations, Test Strategy, Trade-offs & Alternatives, Risks & Mitigations, Open Questions for Judge.

## Architect Invocation (Modular-Extensible Strategy)

### Spec Packet
The specification from the previous 'requirements' phase will be provided as context.

### Strategy
modular-extensible

### Instructions
Propose a modular and extensible architectural approach. Clean interfaces, dependency injection, plugin points, future-proofing. Query the scout agent for existing patterns, interfaces, and dependencies. Return an Architecture Design Doc with: Strategy, Goal Restatement, High-Level Approach, Component Diagram, File Change Plan, Data Models & Schemas, API/Interface Definitions, Key Algorithms (pseudocode), Dependency Changes, Configuration Changes, Error Handling & Failure Modes, Concurrency & State Considerations, Security Considerations, Test Strategy, Trade-offs & Alternatives, Risks & Mitigations, Open Questions for Judge.

## Architect Invocation (Edge-Case-Focused Strategy)

### Spec Packet
The specification from the previous 'requirements' phase will be provided as context.

### Strategy
edge-case-focused

### Instructions
Propose an edge-case-focused architectural approach. Explicit handling of failure modes, partial states, concurrency, limits. Query the scout agent for existing patterns, interfaces, and dependencies. Return an Architecture Design Doc with: Strategy, Goal Restatement, High-Level Approach, Component Diagram, File Change Plan, Data Models & Schemas, API/Interface Definitions, Key Algorithms (pseudocode), Dependency Changes, Configuration Changes, Error Handling & Failure Modes, Concurrency & State Considerations, Security Considerations, Test Strategy, Trade-offs & Alternatives, Risks & Mitigations, Open Questions for Judge.

phases.synthesisPrompt:
## Architecture Judge Synthesis

Compare the three proposals above (minimal-diff, modular-extensible, edge-case-focused) against the acceptance criteria from the 'requirements' phase. Query the scout agent to verify disputed technical assumptions. Evaluate on: AC Coverage (30%), Spec Compliance (20%), Codebase Fit (15%), Risk Mitigation (15%), Maintainability (10%), Implementation Effort (10%).

Synthesize a single, actionable, step-by-step implementation blueprint for the Coder. Return an Implementation Blueprint with: Selected Approach, Decision Matrix, Scout Verification Results, Rationale, Rejected Elements, Implementation Blueprint (Phases: Foundation, Core Logic, Integration & Wiring, Tests with file/action/details), Acceptance Criteria Traceability, Risk Mitigations in Blueprint, Open Questions for Coder.

tasks.prompt:
## Coder Invocation

### Implementation Blueprint
The blueprint from the previous 'architecture_ideation' phase synthesis will be provided as context.

### Spec Packet
The specification from the 'requirements' phase will be provided as context.

### Instructions
Implement the approved changes cleanly in the repository, adhering to existing conventions. Query the scout agent whenever exact signatures, imports, or surrounding module behaviors need verification. Return an Implementation Summary with: Blueprint Reference, Files Modified table (File, Action, Lines Changed, Summary), Implementation Decisions table (Step, Decision, Rationale), Verification Results table (Command, Status, Output Summary), Deviations from Blueprint table (Step, Deviation, Reason, Impact on ACs), Scout Queries Made table (Question, Finding, Step Applied), Open Questions for Reviewer/Release Gate.

tasks.description: Review implementation against spec and blueprint
tasks.prompt:
## Reviewer Invocation

### Spec Packet
The specification from the 'requirements' phase will be provided as context.

### Implementation Blueprint
The blueprint from the 'architecture_ideation' phase synthesis will be provided as context.

### Code Diff
The implementation from the previous 'coder' task will be provided as context.

### Environment Constraints
Static analysis only. No live runtime. No integration environment.

### Instructions
Inspect the Coder's diff against the Tech Lead's specification and Architecture Judge's blueprint. Perform static test and edge-case analysis strictly within the declared environment constraints. Identify concrete bugs, logic flaws, unhandled edge cases, regressions, and missing unit/static test coverage, using the scout agent to check callers and contracts.

### Output Format
Return a Review Verdict with: Overall Status (PASS/FAIL), Traceability Summary table (AC ID, Criterion, Code Implemented, Test Covered, Status), Fix List (if FAIL: ID, Severity, File, Line, Issue, Required Fix), Static Analysis Findings (Non-Blocking), Scout Verification Results, Edge-Case Analysis Summary table, Test Coverage Assessment table, Approval statement.

## Release Gate Invocation

### Spec Packet
The specification from the 'requirements' phase will be provided as context.

### Implementation Blueprint
The blueprint from the 'architecture_ideation' phase synthesis will be provided as context.

### Final Code Diff
The implementation from the 'implementation' phase will be provided as context.

### Reviewer Verdict
The output from the previous 'reviewer' task will be provided as context.

### Coder Implementation Summary
The output from the 'coder' task will be provided as context.

### Environment Constraints
Static analysis only. No live runtime. No integration environment.

### Iteration Count
1

### Instructions
Audit the complete implementation and review history against the original user goal and acceptance criteria. Verify that no requirements were dropped. Either approve and produce the final user-facing delivery summary, or reject the build back to the Coder with specific unmet criteria (within the allowed retry budget).

### Output Format
Return a Release Gate Verdict with: Overall Decision (APPROVED/REJECTED), Iteration (1/3), Acceptance Criteria Audit table (AC ID, Criterion, Code Verified, Test Verified, Static Verified, Runtime Gap, Status), Requirements Integrity, Runtime Verification Gaps table, Reviewer Verdict Alignment, Coder Verification Results, Risk Assessment table, Scout Verification Results. If APPROVED: Delivery Summary with What Was Built, Files Changed, Acceptance Criteria Met, Runtime Verification Required, Known Limitations, Rollback Plan. If REJECTED: Unmet Acceptance Criteria, Blocker Issues from Reviewer, Retry Guidance for Coder.
